Morning comes without any hurry.
The light is very pale.
Coffee fills small warm cups.
A bird taps the glass.
My hands remember old work.
The floor still holds cold.
Outside, the rain has stopped.
I count my slow steps.
The chair accepts my weight.
Day opens like a book.

I step toward the door.
The hallway smells of dust.
Shoes wait near the wall.
I wear my old coat.
The street outside is quiet.
Puddles reflect the broken clouds.
A dog passes by slowly.
My shadow stretches far ahead.
The park bench is damp.
I sit for a moment.

Leaves whisper in the wind.
I watch the tall trees.
Their branches touch the sky.
A memory arrives uninvited now.
I am seven years old.
A mother calls my name.
The sun feels very hot.
We ran through green grass.
Laughter sounds like clear water.
Then the long afternoon ends.

I close my tired eyes.
The past becomes a film.
Faces appear then fade away.
My father teaches me carefully.
He speaks with gentle patience.
His voice holds the world.
I learn to listen closely.
Now he has long gone.
His words remain in me.
They quietly guide my choices.

I rise from the bench.
The city hums softly nearby.
People walk with quiet purpose.
A child chases white pigeons.
Someone carries a wet umbrella.
The air feels suddenly clean.
I breathe deeply one time.
The sun moves very slowly.
My feet find easy rhythm.
I keep walking steadily on.

The river waits far below.
Its current murmurs very soft.
Stones hide beneath the surface.
I think of passing time.
It flows like river water.
We cannot hold the current.
We can only watch it.
And yet we often try.
Small moments build the river.
Each second becomes a stone.

At noon, I stop walking.
A bench faces the bridge.
I place my worn bag.
The bridge creaks high above.
Water shimmers in bright sunlight.
A silver fish jumps briefly.
I feel suddenly less lonely.
The river knows nothing here.
It carries fallen leaves away.
I let my mind rest.

After lunch, I keep walking.
My stomach feels gently full.
The path bends gently right.
Trees make soft green shadows.
A gentle breeze moves leaves.
I smell rain in air.
Dark clouds gather to east.
The wind begins to shift.
My pace quickens very slightly.
I finally reach the square.

Fountains splash inside old stone.
Children play near old benches.
A musician plays soft violin.
Notes float upon the wind.
A woman listens very closely.
I stand quietly and watch.
The music feels very old.
It reminds me of home.
Not the place itself exactly.
But the warm feeling inside.

The square fills with sound.
Voices rise and softly fall.
I almost hear my name.
A stranger smiles at me.
I smile back quite gently.
We do not speak aloud.
Some gestures need no words.
The late afternoon turns golden.
Light touches each visible face.
I feel part of it.

Soon the light begins changing.
Shadows lengthen across the pavement.
I buy a thin paper.
The shopkeeper nods to me.
He already knows my order.
I think this is strange.
We share a small habit.
The ritual keeps us close.
Yet life keeps moving on.
We catch one passing glimpse.

The newspaper carries the news.
I read about heavy rain.
I read about quiet loss.
I read about sudden joy.
Words build small temporary worlds.
I fold the newspaper page.
The city continues around me.
My thoughts move very slowly.
I am not quite sure.
But I keep walking on.

The evening deepens quickly now.
Streetlights blink softly to life.
Windows glow with warm dinner.
The smell of bread returns.
I remember one small kitchen.
A stove ticked very softly.
Someone hummed an old song.
The table held our plates.
Laughter filled the warm room.
Now I carry that warmth.

The walk home begins now.
My legs feel gently tired.
My mind feels strangely bright.
I notice every falling leaf.
I notice every passing face.
I notice every distant sound.
The whole world grows tender.
Fear loosens its small grip.
Gratitude rises without any warning.
I thank the whole day.

I cross the quiet park.
The grass is very cool.
My shoes press down softly.
The earth receives my weight.
A red fox appears briefly.
It watches me from afar.
We share one brief glance.
Then it vanishes into trees.
I feel seen, then free.
The park keeps its secrets.

My house appears dimly ahead.
The key turns very slowly.
The door swings gently open.
The room breathes around me.
I set my wet coat.
I hang it up there.
The silence feels quite friendly.
My feet find the floor.
The floor holds my weight.
I am finally home again.

I make warm tea now.
The kettle whistles softly once.
Steam rises in slow spiral.
I hold the warm cup.
Heat spreads through my hands.
I sit beside the window.
Outside, the darkness has gathered.
Streetlights quietly mark the road.
The city sleeps very softly.
I sip the warm tea.

The night asks no questions.
It waits with deep patience.
My thoughts grow steadily quieter.
I release the long day.
I release my daytime worries.
I release my hidden fears.
The body loosens its tension.
The mind softens its edges.
Sleep waits near the door.
I let it approach slowly.

I think of that morning.
The thin silver line returns.
The kettle whispers gentle warmth.
The bird taps the glass.
My hands remember old work.
The floor still holds cold.
The rain has finally stopped.
I count my slow steps.
The chair accepts my weight.
The new day will begin.

I close my tired eyes.
The night holds me softly.
I am small and here.
I am held by time.
The world turns beyond me.
Tomorrow will ask for care.
I will meet it gently.
I will listen to it.
I will learn from it.
I will let it be.
